memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The sons of Gad... The sons of Asher... These were the children born to Jacob by Zilpah, whom Laban had given to his daughter Leah—sixteen in all." — Gen 46:16-18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Zilpah was a servant girl. She had no status, no choice in how her life was arranged, and no say in becoming part of Jacob's household. She was, in the language of her day, given — passed from Laban to Leah as property.

And God recorded her name in Scripture, alongside her children and grandchildren.

Two of Israel's twelve tribes came from her. Asher's descendants would settle rich land in the north; Gad's would be known as fierce and faithful warriors. These were not second-class tribes. Their portion in the promised land was as real as anyone's.

There is something very godlike about that. Human beings sort people constantly — by birth, by income, by education, by which family they married into. God does not sort that way. He looked at a servant woman with no standing and made her part of the family through whom He would bless the world.

This is exactly what Paul says has happened to us in Christ. There is no longer slave or free, because we are all one in Him, and all heirs of the same promise (Gal 3:28-29). Your standing in God's family does not depend on where you started.

The world's categories do not survive contact with God's grace.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you rank yourself above or below others in ways God does not?
2. How does it change you to know your standing in Christ has nothing to do with your background?
3. Who around you is treated as insignificant that God clearly values?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that in Christ my background does not determine my standing before You. Help me see people the way You see them, and stop measuring anyone by the world's scale. Amen.
